solution.label: Class diagram of the music library redesign
solution.description: Song and Playlist both implement the Playable interface, which declares duration() and play(queue). Song keeps a title and a length in seconds. Playlist keeps a name, offers add(item: Playable), and holds any number of Playable items, so its items may be songs or other playlists.
solution.caption: A dashed arrow with a hollow triangle means a class implements an interface. The arrow with a hollow diamond means a Playlist holds any number of Playables, which may be songs or other playlists.

trace.label: Sequence of one press of Play on Road Trip
trace.description: The Play button, button, calls play(queue) on roadTrip. roadTrip calls play(queue) on throwbacks, which calls play(queue) on its song mixtape.
trace.caption: Lifelines are named like the variables in the main program. The trace follows one path down the tree: Road Trip's two songs and Cassette Heart receive play the same way and are left out. Messages appear as the narration reaches them.
trace.source:
@startuml
participant button: PlayButton
participant roadTrip: Playlist
participant throwbacks: Playlist
participant mixtape: Song
steps:
activate button
button -> roadTrip: play(queue)
activate roadTrip
roadTrip -> throwbacks: play(queue)
activate throwbacks
throwbacks -> mixtape: play(queue)
activate mixtape
deactivate mixtape
deactivate throwbacks
deactivate roadTrip
deactivate button

roles.label: Composite pattern role diagram
roles.description: A Client uses the Component interface, which declares operation(). Leaf and Composite both implement Component. Composite also declares add(child: Component) and holds any number of Components as its children.
roles.caption: This is the safe arrangement, with add only in Composite; the transparent one also declares add in Component. Composite both implements Component and holds Components, so composites can contain composites.

cards.title: Benefit: simple clients
cards.text: Clients treat one object and a group the same way, with no type checks; wherever one item fits, a whole group fits too.

cards.title: Benefit: new kinds fit in
cards.text: A new leaf or group class that keeps the shared interface works in existing structures and with existing clients, unchanged.

cards.title: Liability: overly general
cards.text: A group that inherits the general add cannot use the type system to restrict its children; it needs checks at runtime.

cards.title: Liability: safety or transparency
cards.text: Add only in the composite is checked early but visible to clients; add in the component is uniform, but leaves reject it at runtime.

cards.title: A good fit
cards.text: Items nest inside groups, groups inside groups, and clients should not care which one they hold.

cards.title: Simpler designs
cards.text: No nesting: a plain list. Same data in every item: one class with an optional list of children plays every role.

cards.title: Neighbors
cards.text: Nested views and macro commands are composites. A decorator wraps one object to add behavior; a composite holds many.

cards.title: Podcast episodes
cards.text: Listeners drop episodes into playlists, right next to songs.

cards.title: An episode
cards.text: It has a show, a title, and a length, and it queues as show: title.

cards.title: Your task
cards.text: Name the class you add and every existing line that changes.

cards.title: Context
cards.text: A part-whole hierarchy that nests, whose clients want to treat one object and a group alike.

cards.title: Problem
cards.text: Code that handles single objects and groups separately repeats its loops and type checks, and breaks as new kinds arrive.

cards.title: Solution
cards.text: A Component interface that Leaves implement directly and Composites implement by forwarding to their children.

cards.title: Consequences
cards.text: Simple clients and easy new kinds, at the cost of an overly general structure and a choice between safety and transparency.
